thread.title: Intraday Update: Apple Is Only Thing Between Dow and a Bad Day

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Intraday Update: Apple Is Only Thing Between Dow and a Bad Day
text:
By Ben Levisohn Updated Aug. 1, 2018 2:15 p.m. ET Careful Now. Don't be fooled by the small decline in the Dow Jones Industrial Average . Without Apple (AAPL), which was surging after strong earnings , the blue-chip benchmark would be even lower as trade-war concerns heat up again . And don't look now, but there's a Fed statement coming this afternoon. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...explain how Apple has distorted index returns today;
•...highlight the boost that Campbell Soup (CPB) got from a possible activist campaign;
•...review Fidelity's decision to offer zero-fee funds, and its impact on BlackRock (BLK).
Blinded by Apple Sometimes "nothing to see here" means just that. This is not one of those times.
On first glance, the market doesn't seem to be doing much. The S&P 500 had declined 0.2% to 2809.78 at 12:25 p.m. today, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average had fallen 88.05 points, or 0.4%, to 25,327.14. The Nasdaq Composite was up 0.1% to 7677.93.
The market, though, is far weaker than it looks thanks to Apple . The tech giant, which is closing in on a $1 trillion market valuation , has gained 5% to $199.84 after releasing earnings after Tuesday's close. Apple accounts for just under 70 Dow points, helping to reduce what might have been a bigger drop. It's also the biggest stock in the S&P 500, where just 152 stocks are trading higher. And while tech, with a 0.7% gain, is the best-performing sector in the S&P 500 today, the average tech stock is down 0.1%. In other words, tech isn't strong...Apple is.
It doesn't help that trade wars are back on the front page, with reports that the U.S. is considering raising tariffs on Chinese goods to 25%. "Although reports indicate the news is an attempt by the U.S. to bring China to the negotiating table, Chinese officials said that ' blackmail ' wouldn’t work and that it would hit back if the United States takes further steps," writes Evercore ISI's Dennis DeBusschere , who blames the reports for sinking stocks.
And of course the Fed planned to release its monetary policy statement at 2 p.m. It could help push the 10-year Treasury yield, which traded above 3% earlier Wednesday , higher depending on the tone.
So don't go away. There's still more to see.
Midday Movers BlackRock (BLK) is down 3.4% to $485.45, along with other asset managers like Federated Investors (FII), down 4.1% and Franklin Resources (BEN), down 4.7%, after Fidelity announced new reduced fee structures, including zero-expense-ratio mutual funds.
Illustration: Getty Images Campbell Soup (CPB) is up 2.1% $41.77 following reports that activist investor Third Point has built a small stake in the company.
C.H. Robinson Worldwide (CHRW) is up 2.5% to $94.52 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The transportation company earned $1.13 a share on revenue of $4.28 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.07 billion on revenue of $4.18 billion.
Dropbox (DBX) is up 2.3% to $27.37 after Jefferies upgraded it to Buy.
Newfield Exploration (NFX) is down 3% to $27.86 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The exploration and production company earned 94 cents a share on $679 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 82 cents on revenue of $619.07 million. — Teresa Rivas
